purpose: Proposed (NOT approved) numeric criteria for comparing a future AP-03 candidate against the AP-01 baseline for the SAME forced input. REV4 after REVIEW-EVD-AP-01-003 (AP01-V3-01/02); previous revision after REVIEW-EVD-AP-01-002 (AP01-V2-02).
what_changed_in_rev4: L1 is now per-channel and per-STAGE over the three adjacent pairs the export actually provides. The profile limit sits between iq_before_profile_limit and iq_mode_request, so REV3's iq_before_profile_limit -> iq_requested pair skipped a stage and reported one guessed cause for three.

Only the profile-limit stage is attributed to a named mechanism, on the strength of a statement in src/assist_modes.c. Later stages are reported as RAISED/REDUCED/UNCHANGED without naming floor or gate.
Channels outside the Iq chain (torque_run_native, cadence_control_rpm) no longer inherit an Iq limit verdict.
Shape never excludes a result: a plateau without a demonstrated change at an observed stage is informational (limiting UNKNOWN), not an exclusion.
I1 gained an explicit zero-ripple boundary: new ripple from a flat baseline is a regression, not 'not improved'.
S1 no longer claims that CONFIRMED implies no earlier re-rise, and no longer implies a shorter stop is evidence of better safety or mechanics.
status: PROPOSAL - a pilot goal, not an approved comfort or hardware contract. Master approves or amends before any use in AP-03.
what_changed_in_rev3: The single symmetric |delta| <= 0.05 rule is gone. It was a SIMILARITY test: a candidate improving relative ripple from 0.10 to 0.01 (a 90% improvement) failed it. Criteria are now split into PRESERVATION (the mean must stay put) and IMPROVEMENT (ripple should go down, directionally, never penalised for going down further).
Arithmetic corrected: 0.05 of a 0.097 baseline is ~52%, not the '20-30%' claimed in REV2. The figure is no longer used as a justification at all.
The stop criterion is a MAXIMUM LATENCY plus a separate trajectory check, not a symmetric delta. A candidate that stops sooner is not penalised for stopping sooner.

Low cadence is reported separately as a smoothness/latency trade-off. The Walk 10-60 rpm contract is NOT used as justification: Walk is a different function with its own contract and says nothing about rider-effort tolerance at low pedalling cadence.
Limiting is decided from real cap/floor channel evidence, not from flatness. Flatness is informational and never excludes a case.
Bias is now COMPUTED in results/ap01-metrics.json against an explicitly named reference case, not merely defined.

measured_baseline_used_for_these_numbers.source: results/ap01-metrics.json (REV3 extraction over the 21 accepted CSVs)
measured_baseline_used_for_these_numbers.note: relative_ripple = RMS(iq_ref - mean) / |mean| over the steady window.

criteria.metric: relative mean change of iq_ref for the identical scenario
criteria.reference: the matching case's steady mean in results/ap01-metrics.json
criteria.proposed_threshold: |mean_bias_relative| <= 0.05 (5% of the baseline mean) for cadence >= 40 rpm
criteria.justification: A smoothing change must not quietly deliver more or less assist. 5% is proposed as the working budget because it is well above the run-to-run reproducibility of this harness (bit-identical repeats, so effectively zero measurement noise) and small enough that a rider-perceptible change in assist magnitude cannot hide inside it. It is a budget chosen BEFORE candidates exist, which is the point: REV2 wrongly deferred this until 'another equivalent implementation' could be measured, which inverts the order - a comparison requirement is set before the thing being compared.
criteria.limits: Symmetric here on purpose: both more and less assist are deviations from the baseline behaviour. Applies per scenario with identical inputs, never across different cadences. Not applicable when the case is excluded by L1 below.

criteria.metric: relative ripple reduction of iq_ref for the identical scenario
criteria.definition: ripple_reduction_fraction = 1 - (candidate_relative_ripple / baseline_relative_ripple), via metrics.compare_channel. Positive = improvement; 0.5 means the candidate's relative ripple is half the baseline's.
criteria.reference: the matching case's steady relative_ripple listed above
criteria.proposed_threshold: DIRECTIONAL - lower is better, always. Working pilot target for cadence >= 40 rpm: ripple_reduction_fraction >= 0.50 while P1 holds. Exceeding the target is a better result, never a failure. BOUNDARY (AP01-V3-02): when the baseline window carries no ripple at all, a percentage reduction is undefined - compare the absolute ripple RMS instead. Ripple appearing where there was none is RIPPLE_REGRESSED_FROM_ZERO (a regression, not merely 'not improved'); zero on both sides is UNCHANGED_BOTH_FLAT.
criteria.justification: Master's stated direction for the pilot: smaller relative ripple is better; a working goal of at least 50% reduction with no more than a 5% change in mean. Worked example on the measured baseline: at 72 rpm the baseline relative ripple is 0.097, so the target is candidate <= 0.0485; at 40 rpm baseline 0.165 -> target <= 0.0825; at 120 rpm baseline 0.053 -> target <= 0.0265. Verified against known signals rather than asserted: test_compare_channel_large_improvement_is_not_penalised drives an 80% reduction through compare_channel and requires the verdict IMPROVED_WITHIN_BUDGET.
criteria.limits: This is a PILOT GOAL for choosing between candidates on this forced-input harness. It is NOT a comfort contract, NOT a hardware acceptance criterion, and carries no claim about how a given ripple figure feels on a real bike - u_abs and battery current are zero here and no mechanical response is modelled. A candidate meeting it has not been shown to ride better; it has been shown to compose a smoother request for these inputs.

criteria.metric: same as I1, restricted to cadence < 40 rpm (cad20, cad30)
criteria.proposed_threshold: REPORTED SEPARATELY, no pass/fail gate proposed. Report ripple reduction together with the stop/response latency for the same candidate, as an explicit smoothness-versus-latency trade-off.
criteria.justification: At low cadence a fixed-duration window contains fewer completed crank revolutions, so the baseline ripple is 2-3x the mid-cadence figure for the same torque input. Any smoothing strong enough to reach a 50% reduction there is likely to lengthen the response, and this harness measures both. The trade-off is a decision for the Master, not something to hide inside a single pass/fail number. NOTE: no Walk-based justification is used - the FW143 Walk 10-60 rpm contract governs a different function and does not license a rider-effort tolerance here.
criteria.limits: Two cadences only (20, 30 rpm). No latency counterpart is measurable for a mid-ride effort change yet - the load-step scenarios remain NEEDS_HARNESS_EXTENSION, so the trade-off can currently be reported only against the stop latency.

criteria.metric: time_to_confirmed_zero_s of iq_ref after the scripted stop
criteria.definition: metrics.stop_points(..., zero_tolerance=1.0 Iq count, min_confirm_s=0.10, max_transition_gap_s=0.05). Only a CONFIRMED status yields a number; NOT_REACHED / INSUFFICIENT_OBSERVATION / OBSERVATION_GAP_TOO_LARGE are not latencies and must never be compared as if they were.
criteria.reference: baseline stop_release_cad72: status CONFIRMED, time_to_confirmed_zero_s = 0.20 s, transition bracket [5.195, 5.200] s (one 5 ms sample), observed hold 4.8 s
criteria.proposed_threshold: CEILING, not a symmetric band: candidate time_to_confirmed_zero_s <= 0.25 s (baseline 0.20 s + 0.05 s headroom). A SHORTER stop does not fail this criterion. The decay trajectory is assessed SEPARATELY and is not folded into this number: report excursions_before_confirmation (how many times the channel entered tolerance and left it again before the confirmed stretch) and the stop-time scatter across scenarios.
criteria.justification: Penalising a shorter stop - as REV2's symmetric |delta| <= 0.05 did - is wrong, because this metric's direction is not by itself a quality verdict. The 0.05 s headroom is 10 sampling intervals of the 5 ms export, comfortably above the +-1-sample bracket uncertainty, and small relative to the release_ms=100 / iq_fall_fast_ms=125 tuning that shapes this decay.
criteria.limits: CORRECTION (AP01-V3): a CONFIRMED status does NOT mean the channel never rose again after first entering tolerance. stop_points looks for the LAST stretch that holds to the end of the record and deliberately tolerates an earlier transient zero followed by a rise; that is why excursions_before_confirmation is reported as its own field and must be read alongside the latency. Equally, a SHORTER time to zero is only the direction of one metric on a forced-input harness - it is NOT evidence of better safety or better mechanical behaviour, which this harness cannot observe at all. Valid only while release_ms and the iq_fall_* tuning are identical between baseline and candidate. Single stop event only - restart-before-release and rolling restart remain NEEDS_HARNESS_EXTENSION.

criteria.metric: per-channel, per-stage limit evidence from the three observed stages of the Iq chain
criteria.definition: metrics.stage_analysis() over the three ADJACENT pairs the export actually provides: (1) profile_limit: iq_before_profile_limit -> iq_mode_request; (2) post_mode_request: iq_mode_request -> iq_requested; (3) request_to_allowed: iq_requested -> iq_allowed. Each stage reports only REDUCED / RAISED / UNCHANGED / MIXED. Only stage (1) is attributed to a named cause (the profile Iq limit, max_iq_pct), because src/assist_modes.c states a difference there is max_iq_pct 'and nothing else'. Stages (2) and (3) are NOT attributed to floor or gate without further evidence. metrics.limit_assessment() then judges each channel against the stages UPSTREAM of that channel only.
criteria.reference: measured on the accepted CSVs (window 3.0-8.0 s), correcting the REV3 labels: BOTH floor cases show the SAME two-stage story - profile_limit REDUCED 129-179 -> 7, then post_mode_request RAISED 7 -> 14 (floor 2%) or 7 -> 175 (floor 25%). REV3 called the first case plain CAP_BINDING with a '174 -> 14' pair, which skipped the iq_mode_request stage, used a single row's value as if it were the window, and hid the limit-ordering finding. without_rotation_repro shows profile_limit UNCHANGED (285 -> 285) and post_mode_request REDUCED (285 -> 0), so it is NOT cap limiting either. without_rotation_off_repro carries no assist at all (ZERO_NO_ASSIST). All riding cases: every stage UNCHANGED.
criteria.proposed_threshold: Exclude a CHANNEL from P1/I1 comparison only when an observed stage UPSTREAM of that channel actually changed its value (LIMITED_UPSTREAM), or the window is constant zero (ZERO_NO_ASSIST). Shape never excludes: FLAT_NO_LIMIT_EVIDENCE and PLATEAU_NO_LIMIT_EVIDENCE both report limiting UNKNOWN and REMAIN comparable. Channels outside the Iq chain (torque_run_native, cadence_control_rpm) receive NO Iq limit verdict at all.
criteria.justification: Two successive corrections. REV2 used pp < 0.5 as a saturation proxy, which excluded a perfectly smooth signal - the very outcome the pilot wants - while missing real limiting. REV3 still excluded a plateau on shape alone, although a plateau can equally come from quantisation, a constant input or a change in effort. Exclusion now requires a demonstrated change at an observed stage. Covered by tests: test_perfectly_smooth_signal_stays_comparable, test_plateau_without_limit_evidence_is_not_an_exclusion, test_real_clipping_needs_a_demonstrated_reduction, test_non_iq_channels_get_no_iq_limit_verdict.
criteria.limits: These three stages are the only ones this export makes visible. Other limiters (battery, thermal, speed) are NOT separated by them, so NO_LIMIT_OBSERVED means 'no change at the observed stages', never 'nothing limited anywhere in the chain'. Stage (2) and (3) causes remain unattributed by design; naming floor or gate needs evidence this export does not carry. iq_ref additionally passes a ramp stage that is not observed as a pair here.

explicitly_not_proposed: No threshold for any NEEDS_HARNESS_EXTENSION scenario (load step/release under PAS, restart-before-release, rolling restart, jitter, reverse timing, sensor-invalid): no measured data exists for them, and a number without data would be worse than a named gap.
No comfort, ride-feel or hardware acceptance claim of any kind. Every number here is a request-composition figure from a forced-input harness with u_abs = 0.
